input: Set up a college alumni networking profile online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this means setting up one profile on a specific platform or across multiple platforms changes the effort and steps involved significantly.
Knowing whether the user is networking with alumni from a specific graduating class, major, or the entire university shapes what groups and connections to prioritize.
The user's current career stage (student, recent grad, mid-career professional) affects what information to highlight and how to frame their profile.
Whether the user's college has an official alumni network or platform (e.g., alumni portal, Graduway) determines if they must use a specific tool or can choose freely.
The user's primary networking goal — job searching, mentorship, industry connections, or staying socially connected — dictates tone, emphasis, and which sections matter most.
Understanding what a 'good' profile looks like to the user (e.g., getting inbound messages, landing interviews, finding a mentor) defines what done well means.
Knowing which platform the user wants to start with (LinkedIn, Handshake, university alumni portal, etc.) determines the exact next action to take.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a college alumni networking profile online
gold.taskDescription: Create and optimize an online profile to connect with fellow college alumni for networking purposes.

questions.title: Which platform do you want to set this up on?
questions.description: Identify the specific platform(s) the user intends to use — e.g., LinkedIn, their university's official alumni portal, Handshake, or a dedicated alumni network app.

questions.title: Does your college have its own official alumni network?
questions.description: Determine whether the university provides a dedicated alumni platform (e.g., a Graduway or alumni portal login), which may be required or preferred over third-party platforms.

questions.title: What is your main goal for connecting with alumni?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user is primarily seeking job leads, mentorship, industry knowledge, social reconnection, or something else — this shapes the entire profile strategy.

questions.title: What is your current career stage or situation?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is a current student, a recent graduate, or a mid-career professional, as this affects what to emphasize on the profile.

questions.title: Are you targeting alumni from a specific major or era?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants to connect broadly with all alumni or narrowly with a specific cohort, graduating class, or field of study.

questions.title: Should this cover one platform or several at once?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a plan for a single profile or a coordinated setup across multiple networking platforms simultaneously.

questions.title: What would make this profile feel successful to you?
questions.description: Understand the user's definition of a successful outcome — e.g., receiving connection requests, landing a specific number of informational interviews, or finding a mentor.
